messages:
Rohit (infra): Heads-up: scheduling a rolling soft-reboot for the 'seashore' GPU cohort in us-west2 on Sun 00:30-02:30 UTC. Reason: NIC microcode update + BIOS thermal trim (addresses sporadic tx retries and a misreporting sensor). No PSU power cycles.
Zoe (sre): Copy. What's the blast radius and expected capacity hit?
Rohit (infra): Expect ~9-13% capacity reduction at peak. Plan: drain -> soft-reboot -> node health checks -> uncordon. Cadence: ~1 node every 70s, parallelism=3.
Mika (oncall): That's reasonable if we have warmbackfill. Can the scheduler reserve same-AZ warm GPUs and seed KV/prefix caches?
Omar (scheduler): Reserving 7 warm GPUs in us-west2: seeding job `ops/seed-prefix --pool=seashore-warm --keys=hot50 --threads=5` scheduled 90m before maintenance. After each node rejoin we'll run a 5m hotpath soak against canary pool.
Pri (support): I'll prepare customer notices for tenants with Dedicated reservations and any pinned pools. Draft: "Planned maintenance in us-west2 may cause transient latency spikes and brief capacity throttling 00:30-02:30 UTC. No data loss expected. Contact support for pinned reservation concerns."
Rohit (infra): Add note that we can offer temporary burst credits for enterprise customers if pinned SLA is impacted; routing fallback to eu-west available.
Zoe (sre): Canary plan: 2 canary nodes, shift 4% traffic for 12m, gates: p95 latency < baseline + 40ms, error-rate < 0.6%. If canary breaches, automatic stop + rollback to previous NIC image.
Omar (scheduler): Canary encoded in `jobs/seashore/soft-restart.yaml` with canary_count=2, canary_traffic=0.04, health_checks=[p95<150ms,error_rate<0.6%], max_parallel=3.
Rohit (infra): We'll set routing flag `route_avoid_recent_boot=true` so nodes with uptime <5m are deprioritized. Also add a temporary traffic-weight rule to steer latency-sensitive customers away.
Mika (oncall): Add paging rule: page oncall if free GPUs in region <5 for >4m. Also watch KV cache miss rate >9% for 2 consecutive 1m windows.
Zoe (sre): Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/seashore-softcycle. Steps: ack page -> pause rollout -> ops/rollback_firmware seashore -> rehydrate caches from snapshot. If canary p95 regresses >30ms capture: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/seashore-canary.pcap`.
net-bot: Reminder: verify MTU delta < 2% on canary post-reboot and check if FEC counters changed.
Pri (support): I'll draft a status page entry and support response templates. Ping me final blurb before publish.
Rohit (infra): Cost note: warmbackfill increases short-term GPU-hours and storage IO; estimate ~$1.6k for window. Finance ok under maintenance budget.
Mika (oncall): Also coordinate with networking: request @networking-team to double-check physical link errors and run `ethtool -S` on canary nodes after reboot.
Zoe (sre): If we detect p95 delta > 30ms or MTU delta >2% we stop rollout and run deeper captures. We'll monitor TCP retransmits, NIC rx_errs, and per-node thermal delta on a temporary dashboard.
Omar (scheduler): Timeline: 23:00 seed caches, 00:15 smoke tests, 00:30 canary start, 00:45 evaluate, 00:50 start rolling with max_parallel=3, finish ~02:10, 02:30 final cool-down.
deploy-bot: Job scheduled: `seashore-soft-restart-v2` at 6188888888, dry-run OK.
Pri (support): Draft posted to #customer-success-drafts for review by product/legal.
Rohit (infra): Final ask: react with :thumbsup: to acknowledge. I'll set infra-bot reminders at 2h and 15m.
Omar (scheduler): :thumbsup:
Pri (support): :thumbsup:
Mika (oncall): :thumbsup: I'll be on standby 00:15-02:45.
Zoe (sre): :thumbsup: prepping rollback scripts and temporary dashboard.
Rohit (infra): Thanks team  will post final customer blurb and runbook link after approvals. Anything else?
Mika (oncall): Nothing else. :coffee:
